entries.name: Woodland BDU
entries.summary: Four-color woodland camouflage battle dress uniform. The Army field uniform from the early 1980s until the ACU.
facts: Adopted in 1981 as the Battle Dress Uniform (BDU)
Replaced by the ACU, fielded starting in 2005
A six-color desert version was issued for desert operations

variants.note: Nicknamed the chocolate chip.

entries.name: Pinks and greens

facts: Pink-toned trousers with a dark olive-green coat
Officer combination in World War II

entries.name: Combat Medical Badge (CMB)
entries.summary: Awarded to Army, Navy and Air Force medical personnel assigned or attached to an infantry unit while it is in actual ground combat; later widened to other ground combat units.
facts: Originally the Medical Badge; created by the War Department, 1 Mar 1945; may be awarded retroactive to 7 Dec 1941 (para 8-10a)
Medical personnel of the AMEDD, Naval Medical Department and USAF Medical Service may qualify (para 8-10b)
Battle participation credit alone is not enough; the infantry unit must have been in contact with the enemy (para 8-10b)
Not awarded to general or flag officers (para 8-10b)
Widened to Special Forces medical sergeants from 19 Dec 1989, armor and cavalry units from 16 Jan 1991, and combat arms and combat aviation units from 11 Sep 2001 (para 8-10c)
Soldiers with MOS 18D are no longer eligible from 3 Jun 2005 (para 8-10c)
Second and third awards are shown by one and two stars centered at the top of the badge, between the points of the oak wreath (para 8-10d)
No second award for the same qualifying period in table 8-2 (para 8-10e)
Badge group 1 for order of wear (DA Pam 670-1, para 22-16a)
entries.remember: Medics with the infantry in combat. Created 1 Mar 1945.

attachments.note: Added 2024: CMB plus an expert badge (para 8-7).

entries.name: Where badges are worn (ASU and AGSU)
entries.summary: Badge limits and positions on the service uniforms.
facts: Badges go 1/4 inch above the ribbons, or above the top of the pocket (DA Pam 670-1, para 22-16b(3)(d))
Only one combat or special skill badge from group 1 or group 2 above the ribbons (para 22-16b(3)(a))
Up to three badges above the ribbons or pocket flap (para 22-16b(3)(e))
Only three badges from groups 3, 4, or 5, including marksmanship, below the ribbons (para 22-16b(3)(b))
AGSU: a total of four badges at one time (para 22-16b(2))

Group 1: CIB, CMB, CAB. Group 2: EIB, EFMB, ESB. Group 3: astronaut device, aviator, flight surgeon, aviation, EOD, parachute rigger. Group 4: parachutist, pathfinder, freefall, air assault, diver, space, and Ranger, SF, Sapper tabs. Group 5: driver and mechanic, marksmanship. Group 6: physical fitness (APFU only) (para 22-16a)
entries.remember: Groups 1 and 2 on top, max three above and three below.
sources: DA Pam 670-1, Guide to the Wear and Appearance of Army Uniforms and Insignia, 26 Jan 2021, para 22-16

entries.name: Service stripes
entries.summary: Diagonal stripes on the left sleeve of the dress coat. One stripe for each 3 years of honorable active Federal service.
facts: Authorized: one stripe for each 3 years of honorable active Federal service (AR 670-1 para 21-28, text from an unofficial copy)
Male ASU: golden-lite stripe, 3/16 in wide, 1-5/16 in long, on blue, 3/32 in border; left sleeve, first stripe 4 in from the bottom; each added stripe 1/16 in higher; 45 degree angle
Male AGSU: heritage tan 566 on heritage green 564; both sleeves; each added stripe 1/8 in higher; 30 degree angle
Female ASU and AGSU: stripe 5/32 in wide, 1-1/4 in long, 5/64 in border
Mess uniforms: gold braid, male 1/2 in wide, female 1/4 in wide, variable length
sources: DA Pam 670-1, Guide to the Wear and Appearance of Army Uniforms and Insignia, 26 Jan 2021, ch 21 (read from the copy hosted at home.army.mil/jackson)
Paras 21-28a to 21-28c. The 3-year rule is from AR 670-1 para 21-28 as quoted at ar670.com (unofficial copy); DA Pam text read did not state it

entries.name: Overseas service bars
entries.summary: Small bars on the right sleeve of the dress coat. One bar for each 6-month period of overseas service.
facts: Authorized: one bar for each 6-month period (AR 670-1 para 21-29a, text from an unofficial copy)
Male: golden-lite bar, 3/16 in wide, 1-5/16 in long, on blue, 3/32 in border
Female: golden-lite bar, 5/32 in wide, 13/32 in long, on blue, 5/64 in border
AGSU: heritage tan 566 on heritage green 564
Worn centered on the outside bottom half of the right sleeve; first bar 1/4 in above the sleeve braid (officers) or 4 in above the bottom of the sleeve (enlisted); each added bar 1/16 in higher
sources: DA Pam 670-1, Guide to the Wear and Appearance of Army Uniforms and Insignia, 26 Jan 2021, ch 21 (read from the copy hosted at home.army.mil/jackson)
Para 21-29a to 21-29d. The 6-month rule is from AR 670-1 para 21-29a as quoted at ar670.com (unofficial copy); DA Pam text read did not state it

entries.name: Army Combat Uniform (OCP)
entries.summary: The daily work, utility, and field uniform, in the Operational Camouflage Pattern.
facts: Includes a coat, trousers, tan 499 undershirt, tan 499 rigger belt, socks, coyote leather combat boots, and headgear (para 4-2)
Patrol cap is the standard garrison headgear (para 4-10a(1))
Coat has hook-and-loop fasteners for the flag, insignia, and tapes (para 4-8a)
OCP items replace UCP items as those become unserviceable and on-hand stock runs out (para 4-1b)
entries.remember: OCP: the daily work and field uniform.

variants.label: Maternity work uniform (OCP)
variants.note: A daily work and utility uniform for pregnant Soldiers (para 5-1).

sources: DA Pam 670-1, Guide to the Wear and Appearance of Army Uniforms and Insignia, 26 Jan 2021 (read from the copy hosted at home.army.mil/jackson)

Shirt: heritage tan 566, short- or long-sleeved
Necktie: four-in-hand, heritage green
A clothing bag issue item for enlisted personnel (para 14-1)

variants.label: Maternity version

entries.name: Army Service Uniform (Army Blue)
entries.summary: Army blue service and dress uniform for men and women.
facts: Male Class A: Army blue coat, low-waist trousers, white short- or long-sleeved shirt (para 11-2b(1))
Male Class B: low-waist trousers and white short- or long-sleeved shirt, no coat (para 11-2b(2))
Coat color: Army blue 450 or 150 (para 11-2a(1))
Private through specialist wear no ornamentation on the trousers (para 11-8c(4))
Male is chapter 11, female is chapter 12, maternity is chapter 13
Service stripes go on the left sleeve and overseas service bars on the right sleeve (paras 21-28, 21-29)
entries.remember: Blue coat is Class A. Drop the coat for Class B.

Male blue evening mess uniform is the most formal uniform worn by Army personnel (para 16-6a)
Female: blue mess jacket, blue skirt (knee- or full-length), white formal blouse, black dress neck tab, black cummerbund, black pumps, sheer stockings (para 17-2)

entries.name: Army White Mess uniform
entries.summary: Seasonal black-tie uniform in white. The White Evening Mess is the most formal.
facts: Normally worn from April to October. Clothing zones I and II may wear it year-round (paras 18-1, 19-1)
Male: white mess jacket, black high-waist trousers, white shirt, necktie, white vest (evening only), black cummerbund, black oxford shoes, black socks, white undershirt (para 18-2)
Female: white mess jacket, black or white skirt, white formal blouse, black neck tab, black or white cummerbund, pumps, sheer stockings (para 19-2)
Male white mess is worn for black-tie functions, like the blue mess (para 18-6a)

entries.name: Service stripes
entries.summary: One stripe for each four years of active duty service.
facts: One stripe for each four years of active duty service. Active reserve time in an active status also counts (para 4231)

Male CPO: 7-inch stripes, 3/8 inch wide. Male E-1 to E-6: 5-1/4 inch, 3/8 inch wide. Women: 5-1/4 inch, 1/4 inch wide
Left sleeve; lower end of the first stripe 2 inches from the end of the sleeve; angled 45 degrees; spaced 1/4 inch apart
Enlisted Sailors with 12 cumulative years of service may wear gold stripes instead of red

entries.name: Surface Warfare Officer insignia
entries.summary: Breast insignia for officers qualified as Surface Warfare Officers.
facts: Officers get the 111X/114X designation, or additional qualification designator LA9 if their designator does not change
That designation entitles an officer to wear the SWO insignia under the uniform regulations (NAVPERS 15665I)
An SWO keeps the designation until NAVPERSCOM revokes it
An officer who needs more than 18 months to qualify triggers a report or extension notice to NAVPERSCOM
sources: MILPERSMAN 1210-090, mynavyhr.navy.mil (https://www.mynavyhr.navy.mil/Portals/55/Reference/MILPERSMAN/1000/1200Classification/1210-090.pdf), CH-16, 27 Sep 2006
Picture: Wikimedia Commons (public domain/CC0) - see CREDITS.md

entries.name: Submarine Warfare insignia (Dolphins)
entries.summary: The Dolphins: bow view of a surfaced submarine with two dolphinfish. Gold for officers, silver for enlisted.
facts: Final design approved for wear on 24 March 1924. Captain Ernest J. King proposed it in summer 1923
Shows a bow view of a surfaced O-class submarine with two dolphinfish resting their heads on its bow planes
Officers wore a gold-plated metal pin on the left breast above their ribbons and medals
Enlisted first wore an embroidered cloth version on the right sleeve (1924-47), then on the left breast from 1947. From 1950 they could wear a silver-plated metal pin
entries.remember: Dolphins on a sub. Gold officer, silver enlisted.
sources: Naval History and Heritage Command, Submarine Warfare Insignia (Dolphins), history.navy.mil
Picture: Wikimedia Commons (public domain/CC0) - see CREDITS.md

entries.name: Naval Aviator and Naval Flight Officer wings
entries.summary: Wings for officers designated as naval aviators or naval flight officers.
facts: Eligible officers may be designated by the Chief of Naval Personnel or the Chief of Naval Air Training as naval aviators or naval flight officers
Designation requires completing the course of instruction. Designators are 131X (naval aviator) and 132X (naval flight officer)
Officers must be commissioned line officers in the Navy, Marine Corps, or Coast Guard
The right to wear aviation insignia may be revoked on the recommendation of a naval aviation evaluation board
Picture shows the Naval Aviator badge. The Naval Flight Officer badge is not pictured
sources: MILPERSMAN 1210-010, mynavyhr.navy.mil (https://www.mynavyhr.navy.mil/Portals/55/Reference/MILPERSMAN/1000/1200Classification/1210-010.pdf)
Picture: Wikimedia Commons (public domain/CC0) - see CREDITS.md

entries.name: Naval Special Warfare insignia (SEAL)
entries.summary: Insignia for officers qualified in special warfare.
facts: After required courses, a 118X officer is reported as qualified in special warfare and the designator changes from 118X to 113X
The officer is authorized to wear the NSW insignia, with a 4-year active-duty service obligation from the qualification date
Selection by the SEAL Officer Selection Panel is required. Waivers are not approved for previous in-service drug use
The official text does not describe the insignia design
sources: MILPERSMAN 1210-220, mynavyhr.navy.mil (https://www.mynavyhr.navy.mil/Portals/55/Reference/MILPERSMAN/1000/1200Classification/1210-220.pdf)
Picture: Wikimedia Commons (public domain/CC0) - see CREDITS.md

sources: MILPERSMAN 1220-050, mynavyhr.navy.mil (https://www.mynavyhr.navy.mil/Portals/55/Reference/MILPERSMAN/1000/1200Classification/1220-050.pdf), 27 Sep 2006 (CH-16)

Qualified members may wear the EAWS insignia and add (AW) after their rating, as in AD3(AW)
Needs command recommendation and commanding officer approval
sources: MILPERSMAN 1220-060, mynavyhr.navy.mil (https://www.mynavyhr.navy.mil/Portals/55/Reference/MILPERSMAN/1000/1200Classification/1220-060.pdf)

Qualified members may wear the EWS insignia and use the EWS designator in parentheses after the rate, as in EOD2(EWS)
Members whose NEC is removed for disciplinary or administrative action, or voluntarily, may not wear it

entries.name: Seaman Recruit
entries.summary: Coast Guard E-1. 1 short diagonal stripe on a blue background (non-rate mark).
facts: Grade: E-1
Non-rate mark: 1 short diagonal stripe sewn on a blue background (para 4.A.7)
Stripe color shows the group: white = seaman, red = fireman, green = airman (para 4.A.7)
Worn on the outer left sleeve of the blue service dress coat, midway between shoulder and elbow and between front and back crease (para 4.A.7)
Pay grades E-2 and E-3 also wear a rating designator above the mark (para 4.A.7)
sources: COMDTINST M1020.6K, Coast Guard Uniform Manual (7 Jul 2020), para 4.A.7

entries.summary: Coast Guard E-4. Collar: 1 gold chevron under a silver shield. Sleeve: perched eagle with 1 scarlet chevron.
facts: Grade: E-4
Collar insignia: 1 metal gold chevron for third class, mounted under a silver Coast Guard shield (para 4.A.5)
Rating badge: perched eagle, wings extended upward, head to the eagle's right; chevrons show the pay grade (para 4.A.8)
Chevron color on the badge for E-4 to E-6 is scarlet, background the same color as the jacket; on the Dinner Dress White Jacket the stripes are navy blue on white (para 4.A.8)
A rating emblem sits between the eagle and the chevrons (para 4.A.8)
sources: COMDTINST M1020.6K, Coast Guard Uniform Manual (7 Jul 2020), para 4.A.5
COMDTINST M1020.6K, Coast Guard Uniform Manual (7 Jul 2020), para 4.A.8

entries.name: Presidential Service Badge (PSB)
entries.summary: Marine Corps service and identification badge: A blue enameled disc, 1 15/16 inches in diameter, surrounded by 27 gold rays radiating from the center.
facts: Design: A blue enameled disc, 1 15/16 inches in diameter, surrounded by 27 gold rays radiating from the center. Superimposed on the disc is a gold-colored device taken from the seal of the President, encircled with 50 stars. (para 4007.2a(1))
Wear: Male Marines wear it centered on the upper right pocket of the blue dress coat, service coat and khaki shirts. (para 4007.2a(1))
No more than two service or identification badges are worn on the same side of the uniform (para 4007.1c)
Command identification badges are not worn with the utility uniforms (para 4007.1c)
sources: MCO 1020.34H, Marine Corps Uniform Regulations (1 May 2018), para 4007.2a(1)
Picture: US - Presidential Service Badge.png, Wikimedia Commons, Public domain

entries.name: Office of the Secretary of Defense Identification Badge (OSD ID)
entries.summary: Marine Corps service and identification badge: An eagle with wings displayed horizontally, grasping three crossed gold arrows, with an enamel shield on its breast (blue upper portion, 13 alternating red and white stripes below); a gold annulet bearing 13 gold stars above the eagle and a green enamel wreath of laurel and olive below; all on a silver sunburst of 33 rays, 2 inches in diameter.
facts: Design: An eagle with wings displayed horizontally, grasping three crossed gold arrows, with an enamel shield on its breast (blue upper portion, 13 alternating red and white stripes below); a gold annulet bearing 13 gold stars above the eagle and a green enamel wreath of laurel and olive below; all on a silver sunburst of 33 rays, 2 inches in diameter. (para 4007.2a(3))

Wear: Only personnel assigned to duty in the OSD who received a certificate of eligibility may wear it. On the blue dress coat and service coat it is centered on the upper left pocket; the miniature is 1 1/2 inches in diameter. (para 4007.2a(3))
No more than two service or identification badges are worn on the same side of the uniform (para 4007.1c)
Command identification badges are not worn with the utility uniforms (para 4007.1c)

entries.name: Joint Chiefs of Staff Identification Badge (JCS ID)
entries.summary: Marine Corps service and identification badge: The United States shield (blue upper portion, 13 red and white stripes) on four gold unsheathed swords, surrounded by a gold scroll with "JOINT" at the top and "CHIEFS OF STAFF" at the bottom in blue enamel letters, all within an oval silver laurel wreath 2 1/4 inches high by 2 inches wide.
facts: Design: The United States shield (blue upper portion, 13 red and white stripes) on four gold unsheathed swords, surrounded by a gold scroll with "JOINT" at the top and "CHIEFS OF STAFF" at the bottom in blue enamel letters, all within an oval silver laurel wreath 2 1/4 inches high by 2 inches wide. (para 4007.2a(4))

Wear: May be permanently awarded to a Marine assigned to the JCS organization who serves at least 365 consecutive days after 14 January 1961 and receives a certificate of eligibility. Worn in the same manner as the OSD ID badge; the miniature is one third smaller with nine stripes on the shield. (para 4007.2a(4))
No more than two service or identification badges are worn on the same side of the uniform (para 4007.1c)
Command identification badges are not worn with the utility uniforms (para 4007.1c)
